parcalar.metin: [excited, emphatic science storyteller] A satellite launched in 1958... is still circling above our heads!
Its name is Vanguard 1. The first satellite to get its electricity from solar cells.
This tiny sphere, about the size of a grapefruit, kept sending signals for more than six years thanks to its solar-powered transmitter.
Its signals went silent in 1964, but the satellite never fell. Today it's still the oldest human-made object in orbit.
Calculations say it won't re-enter the atmosphere until the late twenty-second century.
[excited] The space adventure of solar panels began with this little sphere. Follow Kozmos Lab!
